show: MLW Fusion — A New ERA Begins (2-Hour Season Premiere)
context: The relaunch broadcast — Fusion returns to weekly TV (free on YouTube) for the first time in 3 years, as a special 2-hour premiere that packages TWO in-story episodes: hour two opens 'we saw a week ago Matt Riddle slithered in to sign the open contract.' Curated as one show (it is one broadcast artifact, yt xMGZfQABDdg) with the episode seam noted at seg-09. Post-Battle Riot 8 canon established here: Contra Unit hijacked the Riot and destroyed defending champion Mads Krueger (steel spike, body bag); Killer Kross outlasted 39 to win the World Heavyweight title. In-story timeline: hour 1 → hour 2 (+1 wk) → 6/6 episode (+1 wk, Shotzi/Nakajima) → Kross–Riddle 2 (+2 wks, 6/13). Women's title canonically the Featherweight championship (also announced as Women's World Championship). Hand-curated from full transcript (auto-captions; names normalized via mlw.com/roster: Zamaya not 'Somaya', Bocchini, Coffey).

segments.outcome: Battle Riot 8 recap opens the new era: Contra Unit hijacked the 40-man Riot and eliminated defending World Champion Mads Krueger; Kross and Riddle fought 'joined at the hip' to the final six; Hammerstone's 'destroyer mode' ended; Kross withstood 39 contenders — 'He's the champion. He's the champion.'
segments.register: the coronation flashback — a new era declared from the wreckage of the old
segments.notes: Establishes the season's three load-bearing facts in 90 seconds: Kross is champion, Contra destroyed the old champion to do it (unknowingly crowning Kross), and Riddle stood beside Kross at the end — the friendship the title will now wedge apart.

segments.outcome: Shotzi Blackheart def. Priscilla Kelly (top-rope senton) — stays undefeated in MLW. Kelly ('hell's favorite harlot', called Shotzi a 'brand parasite') controlled stretches with Kawada kicks and a half-and-half suplex. Post-match, Shotzi to Bocchini: 'I want a shot at the MLW Featherweight Championship... Shoko, I know you're at home watching in Japan. Your time is up.'
segments.register: two sides of the same rebellious coin — the winner earns the kaiju
segments.notes: The challenge that becomes the 6/6 title change. Commentary seeds both contenders as Nakajima challengers; the loser (Kelly) keeps her spotlight-hunting thread open.

segments.outcome: Orlando press conference package: MLW CEO Court Bauer on camera introduces the new champion. Kross announces the OPEN CONTRACT: 'Anybody in the world can sign this and face me... I'm going to suplex you on your head. I'm going to leave you where I find you. Tick tock.' Plus the Don Gato celebrity bit (Danny McBride, Steve Little; Los Tekkas body-bagged for touching the tequila).
segments.register: the champion throws the door open — confidence as format
segments.notes: The open contract is the season's first storytelling engine: an anyone-can-sign stipulation that turns 'who signed?' into the episode-long hook. Bauer presenting it on camera = the company formally blessing the new era.

segments.outcome: Hammerstone, to Bocchini: 'That title that I've been chasing ever since I came back is stained with MY blood, MY sweat, and MY tears. I'm going to go sign it.' — then learns the contract has ALREADY been signed. 'WHO SIGNED IT?'
segments.register: the displaced king beaten to the door
segments.notes: The fury that fuels his hour-two main event and the 6/6 'my championship' segment. Beaten to the contract = the franchise rendered an afterthought in one beat.

segments.outcome: Scarlett Bordeaux def. Aaliyah James (Scarlet Ladder) — undefeated since her return. Post-match show of respect for the Essex debutant ('bad girl gone good,' per commentary).
segments.register: the smoke show in her own right — the power couple's other half builds her own ledger
segments.notes: Commentary ties her run explicitly to Kross's: 'a new pedestal... but that just makes them targets.' The pair's parallel undefeated/championship arcs are being built as one household story.

segments.outcome: Krueger package, deeper cut than the 6/6 version: 'The message came from the serpent. You have to answer him now.' / Krueger: 'I was paid well to wave the black flag. But that was never my cause. Where I go now, I go alone.' Battle Riot detail: a reinforced Contra — Ikuro Kwon, Simon Gotch, and a gargantuan wearing one of Mads' old masks — eliminated him, spiked him unconscious, and body-bagged him.
segments.register: the serpent's collection — independence priced in steel
segments.notes: 'The serpent' = Contra's unseen director, the season's shadow authority. The gargantuan-in-Mads'-mask detail is a planted mystery (someone wears the old monster's face). One additional Contra name garbled in captions ('Baba Thunder') — left unattributed rather than guessed.

segments.outcome: Hour-one MAIN EVENT: Austin Aries def. Trevor Lee (brainbuster) in a 'best belt bonus' classic (the boss paid both extra). Lee — returned at Battle Riot 8, repackaged 'thinking man's' version — hung step-for-step. Post-match promo: Aries runs his resurgence ledger (Kushida, Paul London, now Lee), calls the Místico loss 'a fluke,' then challenges BLUE PANTHER for the National Openweight title: 'I want to end your illustrious career... sign the contract and defend your title against the one, the only Austin Aries.'
segments.register: the comeback that demands a legend's scalp
segments.notes: The Blue Panther challenge originates HERE — the 6/6 Bocchini/tortillas segment is its second beat. Mistico named as unfinished business links this thread to the lucha spine. Carrier Blue Panther listed for the challenge, not the match.

segments.outcome: Hour-one closer: the open contract's signer revealed — 'THE RUDE DUDE JUST MADE IT OFFICIAL. We're getting Kross 2.' Matt Riddle, Kross's former friend and sparring partner, takes the first title shot.
segments.register: the friend takes the shot — the wedge driven on night one
segments.notes: Hour two adds Riddle's words: 'You might have beaten me once... I'm taking back MY MLW Heavyweight Championship' — Riddle is a former champion and holds a prior loss to Kross. The hype package codifies the history: friends who wagered on choking each other out.

segments.outcome: HOUR TWO opens (in-story: one week later). With the Skyscrapers invading the commentary booth, Good Brothers def. the Coffey Brothers (Mark & Joe, w/ Wolfgang — MLW tag debut, Glasgow ex-rugby 'designer violence') via Magic Killer. Post-match: full four-man brawl with the watching champions — Dijak: 'They might have won the battle, but they're not going to win the war. I've seen enough.' Sets the title tables match for next week (the 6/6 main event).
segments.register: three packs circle one set of belts — the booth as a throne under siege
segments.notes: The Skyscrapers-on-commentary device lets the champions narrate their own siege ('we are the pinnacle') while two challenger teams collide below. Coffeys eye the belts on debut — a third team banked into the tag division's war.

segments.outcome: Don Gato origin-story vignette (w/ Danny McBride & Steve Little): grief, Vegas, complimentary tequila — 'he could feel his power returning... TEQUILA POWER' — all-on-black, an agave field in Jalisco, the Don Gato Tequila empire. 'Origin story, baby.'
segments.register: the sponsor as folk hero — comedy lane with its own mythology
segments.notes: Resolves the 6/6 tequila vignette (garbled in that episode's captions): Don Gato is a recurring masked comedy/sponsor character with celebrity-fan satellites. MLW running an unapologetic merch-myth lane alongside the violence.

segments.outcome: Diego Hill def. Adam Brooks (standing Spanish fly → corkscrew 'Dive Bomb') — survived the 'loose ledge' Australian's focused-rage striking game, fought back from concussed-and-limp to win ugly. Commentary: 'I don't know if Diego Hill ever truly down-in-the-dirt earned a win as much as this.'
segments.register: the prospect's first war — pretty wins are over
segments.notes: Backstory canon: brother found wrestling first, Diego followed; 'rags to riches he still writes every time.' This gritted-out win is what earns the Místico match one week later — the ascent thread opens here.

segments.outcome: Shoko Nakajima, via satellite from Japan, ACCEPTS Shotzi's challenge — Featherweight/Women's World title match official for next week's Fusion (the 6/6 title change). 'She's a fighting champion.'
segments.register: the kaiju answers — one-week build to a throne change
segments.notes: Clean two-beat construction: challenge (hour one) → acceptance (hour two) → match (next episode). Skein's promised-payoff ledger gets its first MLW paid-in-full receipt.

segments.outcome: ZAMAYA's MLW debut: destruction of Carolina Cruz (Killer Bomb; ringside mats pulled for a DVD on exposed concrete). 'I'm not sure where she came from. I don't know what her background is. All I know is the here and the now.' Crowd 'doesn't know what to think.'
segments.register: the destroyer's calling card — no past, only consequence
segments.notes: Also includes the Contra hacked-feed interruption just prior ('Contra has hacked our feed once again') — the faction's signature device re-established. Zamaya debuts the same fortnight the featherweight throne changes: collision course with the Shotzi reign built into the calendar.

segments.outcome: Kross–Riddle 2 hype package: 'once friends, once sparring partners, used to have a friendly wager over who could choke out the other... now the desire of being world champion comes between what was once a close bond.' Title match set for two weeks out (6/13). Riddle promo mocks Hammerstone ('cry like a big oversized baby') and claims the belt as his to take back.
segments.notes: The 6/6 closing package re-airs much of this material (including Kross's press-conference 'open contract I signed earlier today' line — which the 6/6 curation initially mis-attributed to Riddle; corrected against this source).

segments.outcome: Hour-two MAIN EVENT: Alex Hammerstone def. Bishop Dyer (stacked-up powerbomb) after the Good Brothers ran in on Dijak at ringside, stranding Dyer mid-match. Hammerstone — 600+ day former World Champion, Battle Riot AND Opera Cup winner, the self-styled 'franchise' — takes the scalp of one half of the tag champions.
segments.register: the franchise reloads on a champion's scalp — hate as fuel
segments.notes: Canon: MJF name-dropped as the friend who 'helped Hammer realize the hate that lives in his heart.' The GB run-in folds the tag war into the singles main event — three threads touch one finish. Hammerstone's path back to 'his' title now runs through whoever survives Kross–Riddle.
